case_title: KUMAR v. STATE OF TAMIL NADU
aggravating_circumstances: Rape followed by double murder, threat to witness, intent to screen the offence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 376, 302, 302 read with 201 and 506 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the brother-in-law of the deceased, attempted to have sexual intercourse with his sister-in-law when she resisted, he struck her on the head with a weapon causing her to fall unconscious. He then had sexual intercourse with her and later attacked her 13-month-old daughter, causing her to become unconscious as well. The accused then poured kerosene on both the deceased and her daughter and set them on fire, resulting in their deaths. The accused arranged for kerosene from a neighbor, threatened her to make a phone call impersonating the deceased to PW-1, and caused the disappearance of evidence. The prosecution established the sequence of events through the testimony of witnesses, medical reports, and forensic evidence, including the presence of semen in the brief of the deceased's daughter and the pattern of burns indicating the cause of death was not suicide.
